statements.sentence: The door `gate-wall-door` starts closed; when it opens, whoever opened it and every creature who can see the door learn the fact `gate-opened`.

The door `gate-wall-door` is held by the posts of Guard (gate-1), Guard (gate-2) and Guard Captain (captain). Each holds it only while posted: in a state its post names, up, and standing on one of that post's cells. The door stays barred to a walker while any one posted holder not allied with the walker does not let that walker through; one holder letting them through is not enough while another posted holder bars them.
The prop Altar (altar) cannot be carried.

The prop Altar (altar) offers something to do: the thing to do “You examine the altar.” (`examine`); the one who does it is told “You examine the altar.”. Nobody hears it; whoever sees them sees it done: one shown the prop Altar (altar) is told the doer “looks the altar over”, one not shown it only that something was done where they stand. It is a checked line: it costs an action, one round of the world out of a fight.
To win the thing to do “You examine the altar.” (`examine`), the speaker rolls Religion against DC 12; beating the DC wins the line and missing it misses.

On a win of the thing to do “You examine the altar.” (`examine`), the one who did it and every witness shown the prop Altar (altar) are told “The sigils are the Pale One’s. The king keeps a shrine to it.” and the one who did it and every witness shown the prop Altar (altar) learn the fact `king-is-cultist`.
On a miss of the thing to do “You examine the altar.” (`examine`), the one who did it and every witness shown the prop Altar (altar) are told “Old stone, old candles.”
The prop Grate by the Hearth (grate) cannot be carried.

The prop Grate by the Hearth (grate) offers something to do: the thing to do “You lift the grate and take the way up.” (`to-chapel`); the one who does it is told “You lift the grate and take the way up.”. Nobody hears it; whoever sees them sees it done: one shown the prop Grate by the Hearth (grate) is told the doer “lifts the grate by the hearth and climbs down into the dark”, one not shown it only that something was done where they stand. It is hidden by the secret `kitchen-passage`: a watcher who sees it done, and sees where it stands, comes to know the secret by sight and is shown it. It is a plain line: it rolls nothing, cannot be missed, and costs nothing on either clock.
When the thing to do “You lift the grate and take the way up.” (`to-chapel`) is done, nothing is answered in words, and the row does what the next sentence says.

When the thing to do “You lift the grate and take the way up.” (`to-chapel`) is done, the speaker is set down on the first free cell of Chapel (region-chapel), without walking the way between, and is told “The tunnel climbs, and you come up through a flagstone behind the chapel's altar.”. One round passes on the world clock with it, and creatures due in it act. Whoever saw the speaker leave is told they went, never where; whoever sees them arrive is told they arrived, never from where. A speaker in a fight, held, or with no free cell to land on is refused the line whole; nobody else goes with them.

In `ready`, `back-to-gate`, `cowed`, `in-hall` or `turned`, on its turn in a fight → acts from its `time` rows.
In `back-to-gate`, on its time (out of a fight) → acts from its `back-to-gate` rows.

In `in-hall`, on hearing a sound (a character's line at once), if what it heard was a claim that failed and it holds `admitted` about the one it heard (it knows who only by seeing them) → to `back-to-gate` (“an admitted guest lied to him”).
In `in-hall`, on its time (out of a fight) → acts from its `in-hall` rows.
Rows (one whose conditions hold is picked by weight):
`approached`: says “You there. Nobody passes this gate without my say. Speak.”
`back-to-gate`: if it knows of no enemy → walks to q -4, r 8.
`barred`: says “Not one step further without my say.”
`in-hall`: if it knows of no enemy → walks to q 3, r -9.
`time`:

One of the bundle `revenger`'s rows by weight: [if it holds that the deed `attacked` was done to it within the last 2 rounds → attacks whoever attacked it; if it holds that the deed `attacked` was done to it within the last 2 rounds → walks to whoever attacked it].
If it knows `guards-turned` and it knows of no enemy → walks to the nearest ally of it.
If an enemy is in reach → attacks the enemy.
If it sees an enemy, none in reach → walks to the enemy.
